seats.label: Claude Code
seats.detail: this column asks before every tool call: y approves, n denies, and nothing runs until you answer. Reads, globs and routine shell commands are answered yes for you, by council rather than by the CLI. Your own settings stay loaded for this seat — your deny rules and your own hooks are in force — because council's own hook asks first and an ask beats an allow rule underneath it

seats.label: Codex
seats.detail: app-server · asks · unmeasured at 0.152.1: this column may edit and run things in the workspace above. Containment is that directory, not a flag — point council at a worktree if that matters. --read opens a room that only talks. This seat is one live `codex app-server` process, opened with approvalPolicy on-request, so the vendor asks when it wants more than the workspace-write sandbox allows — and that request is an approval card here, answered down the same pipe. It does not ask about a write inside the workspace. The boundary is still the directory, not the cards, and nothing on this shape has been watched running: read from the vendor's docs, not from a live turn. If the app-server handshake is refused the seat falls back to `codex exec --json`, which asks about nothing

seats.label: Antigravity
seats.detail: stream-json · unasked · unmeasured at 1.1.24: this column may edit and run things in the workspace above. Containment is that directory, not a flag — point council at a worktree if that matters. --read opens a room that only talks. This seat is one live `agy --input-format stream-json` process that stays open across turns, and NOTHING on that channel asks: the envelope carries prompts, a hook that answers `ask` has nobody in print mode to answer it, and every write is unasked. The workspace above is the containment, exactly as on the measured `-p` invocation it falls back to. The boundary is still the directory, not the cards, and nothing on this shape has been watched running: read from the vendor's docs, not from a live turn

seats.label: Cursor
seats.detail: this column may edit and run things in the workspace above. Containment is that directory, not a flag — point council at a worktree if that matters. --read opens a room that only talks. This seat sometimes asks first, and the room answers: its ACP server raises an approval card for a shell command its own allowlist does not cover. It does NOT ask about file edits — measured twice, it wrote a file with no card, in a directory it had never been told to trust. The boundary is still the directory, not the cards

seats.label: Grok
seats.detail: acp · asks · unmeasured at 1.0.13: this column may edit and run things in the workspace above. Containment is that directory, not a flag — point council at a worktree if that matters. --read opens a room that only talks. This seat is one live `grok agent stdio` ACP process, and a permission request it raises is an approval card here, answered down the same pipe. Whether it raises one before a write at all is unknown: on the measured invocation (`--single`) it wrote with no request under every flag tried. The boundary is still the directory, not the cards, and nothing on this shape has been watched running: read from the vendor's docs, not from a live turn. If the ACP handshake is refused the seat falls back to `--single`, which asks about nothing and is where its cost figure comes from
